sources.title: Spider-Man: conheça os 6 principais jogos do Homem-Aranha
sources.text: Muitos personagens dos quadrinhos ganharam destaque nos videogames ao longo dos anos, mas não dá para negar que nosso querido Homem-Aranha é um dos mais emblemáticos. Desde os tempos do Atari, no início dos anos 1980, o herói já ganhou dezenas de adaptações, para todo tipo de plataforma e com resultados muito variados. Por muito tempo, os jogos do Aranha oscilaram entre aqueles mais apressados para casar com o lançamento de filmes e experiências mais ambiciosas, que tentavam capturar o que torna o herói único: a sensação de balançar entre os prédios de Nova York, a agilidade nas lutas e o peso emocional de ser Peter Parker. Nem todos os jogos, porém, ficaram na memória dos fãs. Alguns definiram o que se espera de um game do personagem, seja pela liberdade de exploração, pela fidelidade ao espírito dos quadrinhos ou pela qualidade da narrativa. Por isso, separamos os principais jogos do Homem-Aranha em ordem cronológica . Confira! Há inúmeros jogos inspirados no herói mais querido da Marvel, então optamos por listar os que são considerados os principais. Lançado pela Activision e desenvolvido pela Neversoft, o Spider-Man de 2000 foi o primeiro grande sucesso do herói na era 3D . Chegou ao PlayStation, Nintendo 64 , Dreamcast e PC, e apostou em uma história original que reunia parte da galeria de vilões do herói, como Doutor Octopus, Venom e Carnage, em uma trama inspirada em um desenho animado dos anos 1990. O jogo ganhou destaque também pela presença de Stan Lee, que aparece como ele mesmo na narrativa. O jogo ainda era linear, dividido em fases, mas transmitia bem a acrobacia e o clima de aventura de uma revista em quadrinhos. Para muita gente, foi a primeira vez que um game do Aranha realmente parecia à altura do personagem, e ele abriu caminho para o que viria depois. Baseado no filme de Sam Raimi, com Tobey Maguire no papel principal, Spider-Man 2 é lembrado até hoje como um dos maiores marcos da franquia , e o motivo tem nome: liberdade. Desenvolvido pela Treyarch, o jogo colocou o jogador em uma Nova York aberta, que podia ser explorada livremente, com missões paralelas, criminosos aleatórios para deter e cidadãos para ajudar. O grande diferencial era o sistema de balanço. Em vez de atirar teias em um ponto fixo do céu, o herói realmente se prendia aos edifícios, com controles que davam a sensação de física e de peso. Até hoje, muitos fãs afirmam que essa foi uma das melhores representações do movimento do Aranha até a chegada da nova geração de jogos. Tobey Maguire e Alfred Molina, o Doutor Octopus, emprestaram suas vozes aos personagens , o que reforçou a ligação com o filme. Também desenvolvido pela Treyarch, Web of Shadows adotou um tom mais sombrio e maduro que os títulos anteriores . A história mostra Nova York invadida por criaturas simbióticas, e o jogador precisa lidar com a ameaça enquanto se relaciona com aliados como Mary Jane, Gata Negra e Wolverine, além de enfrentar Venom. O ponto mais marcante era o sistema de escolhas. Ao longo da campanha, o jogador decidia entre o caminho do herói e a influência do simbionte, alternando entre o traje clássico e o traje negro, e essas decisões alteravam parte da narrativa e o final do jogo. O combate ágil, com combos aéreos e golpes em paredes, também ajudou a consolidar o título como um dos favoritos de quem cresceu na era do PlayStation 3 e do Xbox 360. Depois de anos de altos e baixos, o Homem-Aranha finalmente recebeu um tratamento de superprodução com Marvel’s Spider-Man, da Insomniac Games , lançado em 2018 para PlayStation 4. A história acompanha um Peter Parker já experiente, com oito anos de carreira como herói, tentando equilibrar a vida pessoal, o trabalho e a luta contra o crime enquanto uma nova ameaça, liderada por Mister Negative e envolvendo figuras como Kingpin e Doutor Octopus, ameaça a cidade. O jogo brilha por combinar quase tudo o que os fãs esperavam: uma Nova York detalhada, um sistema de balanço fluido e viciante, um combate inspirado nos jogos do Batman da série Arkham e uma narrativa emocional , que trata Peter e Otto Octavius com surpreendente profundidade. Vendeu mais de 20 milhões de cópias, ganhou uma versão remasterizada para PlayStation 5 e chegou ao PC em 2022, o que ampliou ainda mais seu alcance. Lançado como título de estreia do PlayStation 5, Miles Morales continua a história da Insomniac , mas troca o protagonista. Agora, o foco é o jovem Miles, que acaba de herdar os poderes de Peter Parker e precisa proteger o Harlem e sua comunidade durante um inverno rigoroso em Nova York. Sua identidade é marcada por habilidades próprias, como os ataques de bioeletricidade, chamados de “Venom”, e a capacidade de camuflagem. Com uma campanha mais curta que a do jogo de 2018, mas igualmente intensa, o título se destaca pelo carisma do protagonista, pelo tom mais pessoal da história e pelo visual impressionante para a época. A trama envolve a corporação Roxxon e o Tinkerer, e mostra que o legado do Aranha pode ser carregado por mais de uma pessoa. O terceiro capítulo da série da Insomniac chegou ao PlayStation 5 em 2023 e elevou a escala da franquia. Pela primeira vez, o jogador alterna livremente entre Peter Parker e Miles Morales , em uma Nova York ampliada, que agora inclui os distritos do Brooklyn e do Queens. As novas asas de teia e os túneis de balanço rápido tornaram a exploração ainda mais dinâmica. A história traz Kraven, o Caçador, e uma das versões mais fortes de Venom já vistas nos games , com Tony Todd na voz do simbionte, além do impacto do traje negro sobre Peter e de seu conflito com Harry Osborn. O jogo vendeu mais de 10 milhões de cópias e chegou ao PC em janeiro de 2025. É considerado por muitos o ponto mais alto da franquia até agora, tanto pela ambição da narrativa quanto pela evolução das mecânicas. Gostou de conferir os principais jogos do Homem-Aranha? sources.title: Nintendo has "no plans to ditch physical games," exec says amid PlayStation disc backlash
sources.text: "We know how much the fans like it as well, so our position has been to be agnostic" Nintendo's vice president and general manager for Latin America, Bill van Zyll, says that the company has no plans to ditch physical media. Physical media has become a big talking point in the last couple of years. Last year, Nintendo caused preservation concerns thanks to the introduction of Game Key Cards – physical cartridges that allow you to download a game, while not holding any of its data. However, Game Key Cards are very much in the rear view window this year with Rockstar Games ' decision to ship GTA 6 exclusively as a code in box release, swiftly followed by Sony announcing it's killing off discs for new PlayStation games in 2028 . Speaking to YouTube creator Coelho no Japão (via Nintendo Everything ), Van Zyll is asked about Nintendo's stance on physical media in the wake of PlayStation's decision, with him responding, "Historically, we've been very agnostic, right? We go off what the consumer prefers, and take that into account very heavily." He then cites that "we also have a platform that was just launched," noting the Switch 2's ability to play both physical and digital games. "There's no plans to ditch physical," Van Zyll explains. "We know how much the fans like it as well, so our position has been to be agnostic." However, unfortunately, that's of course only the stance right now, and there's no telling what the future holds, but hopefully Nintendo will stick with it for a while longer. Given that every first-party release except for Pokemon Pokopia and the upcoming Hyrule Warriors: Age of Calamity – Definitive Edition have been actual physical releases instead of Game Key Cards, it may be a good sign for now. sources.title: Nintendo executive confirms company has "no plans to ditch physical games"
sources.text: "We go off of what the consumer prefers." Bill van Zyll, VP and general manager for Nintendo in Latin America, has reiterated Nintendo's stance on physical media, confirming that the company has no immediate plans to move to an 'all-digital' future. In an interview with Youtuber Coelho no Japão , van Zyll acknowledges the interest fans have in physical media - reignited lately thanks Sony's controversial decision to announce PlayStation will be discless by 2028 - and says the company will continue to invest in physical media for the foreseeable. "Historically, we’ve been very agnostic, right?" says van Zyll in the interview. "We go off what the consumer prefers, and take that into account very heavily. We also have a platform that was just launched. We're barely just over a year into NS2. It's got both digital and physical – that capability. There's no plans to ditch physical. We know how much the fans like it as well, so our position has been to be agnostic." When van Zyll mentions being 'agnostic' here, he's referring to the fact that the Switch 2 ecosystem revolves around both digital versions of games - primarily purchased via the Nintendo-run eShop - and physical game cartridges that either contain full games or act as 'licenses' that allow you to play digital games when inserted. These game key-cards are not immune from controversy themselves , however: there is often consumer push-back when it turns out the physical version of a game is 'just a key card' . Sony's decision to kill off disc-based games has been met with furore, but recently there have been signs that the company may be considering changing its mind about the move. Developers like Hideo Kojima have given their two cents about the proposition, and even CD Projekt Red has said it'd be powerless to do anything about physical media if Sony decides to stop supporting it. So then, it's nice to see Nintendo publicly support the continued existence of games as physical media. In the current landscape, however, it's hard to predict how long it will stick to its guns on the topic.

sources.title: Unlike Sony, Nintendo Exec Says Switch 2 Maker Has No Plans To Abandon Physical: ‘We Know How Much Fans Enjoy It’
sources.text: Nintendo Nintendo Switch 2 Physical Games Sony has taken a lot of heat for its decision to abandon physical games. Fans spent the summer bombarding PlayStation State of Play livestreams with shouts of “no disc, no buy,” while also creating a list of every time the company had previously claimed that players owned their digital games . Against this backdrop, other hardware manufacturers have tread carefully. Microsoft has kept a neutral stance on whether the company will continue to support physical games with the next-gen Project Helix Xbox devices. Nintendo, on the other hand, is now reassuring its fans that physical games are here to stay, at least on Switch 2. Vice President and General Manager for Nintendo in Latin America Bill van Zyll spoke on the topic during a recent interview with YouTuber Coelho conducted during the Brazil Game Show. The Nintendo-focused YouTube channel asked about a number of topics related to Nintendo’s activities in the region, including localized Nintendo Directs. That’s when the question of physical games inevitably came up. Van Zyll was keen to emphasize the benefits of the format while assuring the companyâs continued plans to produce physical games. âHistorically, we havenât had a preference for a specific format,â he explains. âWe take consumer preferences very much into consideration. We also have a platform that was just launched. Weâve been around for a little over a year with the Nintendo Switch 2, and it offers both digital and physical games. Therefore, we have no plans to abandon physical media. We know how much fans enjoy it.â Notably, consumer preferences favor physical sales on Nintendo platforms more so than those of their competitors. While Sonyâs unit sales share of digital full game downloads versus physical is at 82 percent , Nintendo in its most recent financial report notes its digital sales ratio (calculated as the unit sales of all digital games, including digital-only titles, versus physical sales) at 61.5 percent. Recent U.S. sales data also shows that while many are frustrated with Game Key Cards, which function as pieces of plastic with DRM keys inside, it hasn’t stopped people from buying them . Nintendoâs heavier reliance on physical sales makes any argument for a shift towards digital sales exclusively far weaker, making the choice to continue supporting physical sales an expected response from the company. Still, as Sony continues conversations with a number of companies over their decision, it is at least reassuring for Nintendo fans that the company has no plans to follow Sonyâs lead. sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day Dev Confirms DDoS Attack
sources.text: Gears of War: E-Day suffered a DDoS attack over the weekend, developer The Coalition has said. Players suffered intermittent disconnects and login issues while trying to play the Xbox Series X and S and PC action game, which The Coalition eventually got on top of. It has now confirmed the problems were the result of a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack targeting online services. “Our teams are continuing to monitor and mitigate this activity. We’ll provide updates if there are any significant changes,” The Coalition said . “Thank you for your patience and understanding.” There is a great deal of speculation online about the motivation behind hitting Gears with a DDoS attack, with some pointing to a continued online vendetta against the game for apparently being “woke.” E-Day has a “mostly positive” user review rating on Steam. Whatever the reason (there may be no overarching reason behind the DDoS attack at all), E-Day is now up and running. Last week, Alinea Analytics' head of marketing analysis, Rhys Elliott, reported that E-Day had sold an estimated 230,000 copies in its first week in what was described as a soft start. These unofficial figures, which are not backed by data provided by Microsoft, pointed to Xbox subscription service Game Pass as cannibalizing sales. Earlier this month, the boss of The Coalition responded to reports that staff at the studio were worried they might lose their jobs amid the ongoing cuts at Xbox, promising the next Gears game wouldn’t take as long to make. Eurogamer had reported on internal concern that layoffs would hit The Coalition after the release of E-Day. "The mood is certainly 'let's not celebrate the game until we're three months post launch, just in case,' which is very unusual," one source told the site. "We're just expecting the next wave [of layoffs], or being reorganized under Activision or something later this year," claimed another. Xbox CEO Asha Sharma’s “reset” of Microsoft’s gaming business has seen nearly 2,000 people cut already this financial year, with more to come. A number of studios have left the business or are in the process of closing down. Microsoft has also reorganized its studios, bringing Halo and Sea of Thieves developer Rare under Call of Duty developer Activision, and Grounded developer Obsidian under Fallout developer Bethesda. Of course, Gears of War: E-Day was selected to be an Xbox Series X and S and PC game, ditching any release for a sales-boosting PS5 version. The Coalition studio head Mike Crump recently told the BBC that success for E-Day goes behind sales, saying: "We measure things like, are we showcasing the platform? Are we pushing the hardware to its limits? Are we showcasing what the Xbox is capable of? ...Our goal basically is to be the best-looking game on the Xbox and really show the industry what's possible with our hardware.” Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. sources.title: Gears of War: E-Day server crashes and login problems are because of DDoS attacks, studio says
sources.text: Gears of War: E-Day's servers have been struggling because they've been suffering distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks, apparently - so someone, or some people, have been deliberately trying to overload them. The Gears of War community X account revealed this after a string of updates related to login issues. The account said: "Earlier today, some players experienced intermittent disconnects, login issues, or other service disruptions in Gears of War: E-Day. These issues were due to distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks targeting our online services. "Our teams are continuing to monitor and mitigate this activity. We'll provide updates if there are any significant changes. Thank you for your patience and understanding." The official Xbox account also tweeted : "Service for Gears of War: E-Day is back to normal. Thanks for your patience while we worked to resolve the issue." And it shared a link to track support updates related to this case. The login issues, which caused extended wait times and resulted in server outages - apparently rendering the game unplayable even if you wanted to play the campaign - were first mentioned yesterday . A handful of hours later, these had apparently been resolved , though many comments to the contrary suggested issues remained. It's a bumpy start for what has otherwise been a notable new entry in the Gears series, with Dom awarding Gears of War: E-day four stars in Eurogamer's review - it's a game of contrasts, Dom said. "Though there's still plenty of waist-high cover, ebb-and-flow firefighting, and braindead machismo, Gears E-Day proves that looking back can, indeed, help you look forward, too," Dom wrote. This isn't the first time this year we've seen a game's online portion impacted by DDoS attacks: in January, Arc Raiders and The Finals were hit by "coordinated" DDoS attacks . Around the same time, Final Fantasy 14 was seemingly targeted by similar attacks . It's an on-going issue in games with no simple or easy resolution.

sources.title: Haunted Chocolatier 'More of an Action RPG' Compared to Stardew Valley, ConcernedApe Says
sources.text: Eric Barone, aka ConcernedApe, has briefly discussed the difference between his all-conquering indie game Stardew Valley and his hotly anticipated follow-up, Haunted Chocolatier . Barone announced Haunted Chocolatier back in 2021, but amid ongoing work on his phenomenally successful Stardew Valley, progress on the follow-up has been slow going. Indeed, in June, Barone admitted to feeling somewhat embarrassed to have to keep on saying he was still working away on the game. “Feels kinda dumb posting this same thing over and over, but that’s the reality,” he said at the time. In a new interview with GQ (thanks, Eurogamer ), Barone touched on what to expect from Haunted Chocolatier when it eventually comes out, and it sounds more different from Stardew Valley than I had expected. It’s set in a more “metaphysical” locale, for a start, and in terms of gameplay it’s more of an action RPG. “It is still what I call a town game,” Barone said, “But it’s more of an action RPG — the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights. It's for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly.” In June, Barone admitted fussing over every last detail in a bid to make Haunted Chocolatier as close to perfect as humanly possible . “I am being very thoughtful about every aspect of the game,” he said at the time. “The things in the game which the player will be interacting with or using very often need to be ‘perfect.’ They need to be seamless, clear, intuitive, satisfying, aesthetic.” He used the example of iterating on the recipe book for making chocolates, which sounded like a significant challenge. “To me, it’s not a simple task, as I torture myself over every last detail,” he said. “This is a UI you will be using fairly often, so it has to be perfect. You need to be able to accomplish your goal with the minimal number of clicks. There needs to be just the right amount of data presented to the player: not so much as to be overwhelming, but not so little as to be trivial or mundane. And the way that this data is laid out on the page is crucial… If the data is all clustered together, it will be disgusting to look at. The data needs to be grouped into compelling, intuitive and easy to read/understand groupings. It needs to look appealing and intriguing. And this is just the bare minimum, that players will likely take for granted. If all of that is accomplished then the player is now comfortable while perusing the recipe book. But I want more than just comfort. I want to delight the player. All of this typically requires me to iterate on something several times before I’m satisfied with it.” Barone also explained why he didn't want to show Haunted Chocolatier off too much at this stage of development. “Partly, it feels like I’m serving a half-baked bread. I would rather serve a fully baked bread,” he said. “Also, I know that many parts of the game will likely evolve and change before release, so if I reveal them early, I risk disappointing players if the final product does not match their expectation. Fortunately, I’m in a position where I don’t need to market the game, so I can take my preferred approach.” Haunted Chocolatier is so far without a release date, as is Stardew Valley 1.7 update, which Barone isn’t working on directly. Earlier this year, he explained his current way of working in an interview with IGN . “Well, part of the reason why I've expanded my team a little bit is so that hopefully I can spend more time working on Haunted Chocolatier," he told us in February. "And it's worked out pretty well so far, I would say. On 1.7, the approach we're taking is that I am like, you might say the creative director and I'm involved with like, 'Okay, here's what we're going to do. Here's some of the ideas.' Then I let the team work on that. And then meanwhile, I'm working on Haunted Chocolatier. "At some point in 1.7's cycle, I will get heavily involved, because I feel like my hand needs to touch every part of the game, every aspect of the update. I need to go over it and adjust it or at least approve everything. So it will require a lot of my time anyway, but I think the balance has been a little bit more shifted, so that I can spend more time focused on Haunted Chocolatier. And I think it's been working out pretty good. That's been a big change from the 1.3 update or 1.1 or something where it's completely me. I had no time to work on a new game. So that has changed. "It is difficult because it's hard to shift gears, I guess. If I'm thinking about Haunted Chocolatier, it's difficult to be like, 'Okay, I'm going to one day of the week or two days of the week work on Stardew Valley.' That's not how my brain works. I'm all in one thing or the other. So I've been trying to work on that. I feel like it requires a lot of discipline, which I'm always working to improve on." We interviewed ConcernedApe and chatted about topics such as the addition of two new marriage candidates with 1.7 , the one secret players still haven't found yet , and why there isn't a Stardew Valley TV show yet . We also chatted with the Stardew Valley community about what the game has meant to them over the years. Wesley is IGN's Managing Editor. Find him on Twitter at @wyp100. You can reach Wesley at wesley_yinpoole@ign.com or confidentially at wyp100@proton.me.

sources.title: Stardew Valley creator's new game, Haunted Chocolatier, is "more of an action RPG" than farming sim
sources.text: "It's for the people that go into the mines." Stardew Valley creator Eric Barone, has given a new interview - and finally revealed a little more information about his upcoming title, Haunted Chocolatier. In a wide-ranging interview with GQ , which tackles topics ranging from creative burnout to the importance of 'cosy gaming', Barone also slips in some new information about what we can expect from his highly-anticipated Stardew Valley follow-up. And it's all rather surprising. Per the interview, this game is a much more action-oriented affair than the cosy homesteading of Stardew Valley: "It is still what I call a town game," he told GQ, "but it's more of an action RPG - the main focus is more about adventuring, finding equipment and getting more powerful. There are monsters, there are boss fights." For anyone that's played Stardew Valley, this won't be a massive shock; there is a combat element to the game, though mostly it's sequestered to one portion of the map - the mines that hold some of the game's rarest materials. If you had fun venturing in there at night to fight slimes and horde minerals, you're going to like Haunted Chocolatier, it seems. "[The new game] is for the people in Stardew Valley that go into the mines. That's what I do, honestly," said Barone. Elsewhere, Barone noted that Haunted Chocolatier is a more "metaphysical" experience than Stardew Valley - which makes sense, I suppose, given its connection to the world of ghosts and spirits - and that "no one's playing the game until I'm ready to show it". Hence, there's still no word on a solid release date. The last update we had on the game was all the way back in January, where Barone noted "I'm alive, the game is still in development" , following up previous statements he made alluding to the fact that the world of Haunted Chocolatier is bigger than Stardew Valley. As for when it's coming out? "The bottom line is, I don’t want to give a release date," Barone said at the start of the year. "The game will come out when it's done." If you want to learn more about the man behind one of video gaming's biggest phenomena of the past few generations, I'd urge you to read the full GQ piece: it's a sensitive, comprehensive look at a man that boasts many talents, yet is also humble and grounded. If you're interested in the musical side of his development process, I profiled Barone once in my column at The Guardian.

sources.title: Jogo brasileiro Deep Dish Dungeon traz mergulho nas sombras com gameplay viciante
sources.text: Publicado pela Raw Fury e desenvolvido pelos brasileiros da Behold Studios ( Knights of Pen & Paper , Chroma Squad ), Deep Dish Dungeon é um dungeon crawler que apresenta todos os requisitos para agradar os jogadores que gostam de jogos do gênero sobrevivência e exploração. Passei a última semana explorando masmorras profundas, enfrentando monstros, cozinhando, resolvendo puzzles, fabricando armamentos e quebrando a cabeça para avançar neste jogo que pode se tornar um dos hits indies deste verão. Com lançamento previsto para 13 de outubro, Deep Dish Dungeon chega para PC via Steam , Xbox Series X|S e Xbox Game Pass . Eu recebi cópias do jogo para PC, com as quais pude me aventurar nesta masmorra profunda ao lado de um amigo, experienciando tanto solo quanto multiplayer, para trazer a vocês o meu relato sobre o que os aguarda nesta obscura - mas divertida - aventura. Uma masmorra profunda e sombria da qual nunca ninguém retornou. Você toparia integrar o grupo que irá se aventurar através dessas esquinas obscuras? Se a resposta for sim, seja bem-vindo a Deep Dish Dungeon! O novo jogo da Behold Studios nos apresenta uma aventura de exploração e sobrevivência dentro de uma masmorra originada das ruínas de um antigo reino, mas que agora é habitada por monstros, mistérios e muitos tesouros. Embora a história não seja o elemento principal - assim como outros jogos do gênero -, Deep Dish Dungeon não deixa de entregar o suficiente para que o jogador tenha curiosidade de continuar explorando e conhecendo mais sobre a masmorra. Através de cartas de outros aventureiros e manuscritos podemos nos aprofundar na lore, apenas o necessário para que sejamos integrados ao ambiente e nos sintamos parte daquele ambiente. Mesmo sem uma narrativa complexa, Deep Dish Dungeon tem um charme clássico, se valendo do que já é de conhecimento geral sobre masmorras, exploração, monstros, armas e armaduras medievais. Esse clima conhecido ajuda o jogo a não ter que ficar se explicando ou criando um imaginário, e assim se concentrar no que realmente interessa: o gameplay. O progresso é lento e calmo em Deep Dish Dungeon - e isso é maravilhoso! Nada, absolutamente nada aqui é guiado. Talvez alguém que esteja experimentando um jogo de sobrevivência e exploração pela primeira vez fique perdido no início. Mas não se desespere, logo você pega o ritmo e entra no fluxo do jogo. Deep Dish Dungeon premia a curiosidade, como a própria Behold Studios diz na página do jogo no Steam. Você verá itens para coletar, alimentos para cozinhar e comer, armas que podem ser criadas e melhoradas, tudo parte da lógica para jogos do gênero. O core do jogo é justamente essa sensação de liberdade que faz com o que o jogador tenha que tentar e tentar até chegar na melhor solução. E ela nem sempre é engessada, possibilitando ao jogador experimentar diferentes alternativas para chegar ao mesmo objetivo. Isso fica muito óbvio logo nos primeiros minutos de jogo, quando você se depara com caixas de madeira e tábuas longas dispostas pelo cenário unicamente para que você possa usá-las da maneira mais criativa possível para acessar lugares altos ou trespassar buracos. Ao se deslocar você deve tomar cuidado e sempre carregar uma tocha. Elas tem um tempo útil de vida, ao apagar podem deixar você na completa escuridão, então você deve administrar isso de maneira estratégica. A escuridão é um dos inimigos mais perigosos, escondendo monstros e nos fazendo perder recursos, mas também auxiliando na hora que temos que nos esconder e ser furtivos, pois aqui a iluminação e nossa movimentação podem denunciar a nossa localidade. Outro ponto que devemos ficar sempre atentos é quanto a nossa alimentação e hidratação. Como em todos os jogos de sobrevivência, você deve construir uma combinação adequada de prepararemos de alimentos e água para que sua vida e stamina estejam sempre com valores altos e você possa encarar os desafios com mais vigor. Já o combate é o mais simplista possível: ataca, defende, atira e corre; enfrentando esqueletos, aranhas, morcegos, moreias e escorpiões. E é isso, nada mais - e nem precisa. Lógico que a astúcia do jogador pode implementar um certo molho ao usar o cenário e tentar combinar os ataques com os amigos, quando jogar no cooperativo. Já a progressão é o que mais me encanta, pois temos um grande cenário, que é a masmorra. Ali podemos montar acampamento, cozinhar, montar uma mesa de confecção, guardar nosso alimento para que não apodreça, melhorar nossas armas e armaduras e guardar nosso espólio. No entanto, para além disso, logo no cenário inicial temos muitos locais que não são acessíveis e temos que progredir, conseguir novos itens e voltar para abrir novos caminhos, seguindo o estilo metroidvania. E como disse antes, nada é explícito ou com um pop-up dando dicas do que você deve fazer. Você tem que analisar o que está em volta e procurar uma solução. E isso pode complicar um pouco mais, pois nem mapa temos no jogo. Ou seja, você deve decorar os cenários e os caminhos pelos quais passou. Mesmo no cooperativo, não sabemos onde estão nossos amigos, o que faz com que tenhamos que nos comunicar o tempo todo para nos localizar. A idéia é transformar a exploração em algo orgânico, através de tentativa e erro. Essa é a essência de Deep Dish Dungeon. Deep Dish Dungeon é um jogo de seu tempo. Ele embarca na onda de jogos de sobrevivência cooperativos, consegue se conectar ao gênero e trazer um gostinho nostálgico ao adotar uma estética que remete a jogos com gráficos de eras passadas. Em Deep Dish Dungeon a Behold Studios mostra uma clara evolução, além da ambição de explorar diferentes temáticas em suas obras: Out of Space nos traz caos, risadas e um ambiente aconchegante; já em Cosplay Club temos carisma e complexibilidade no gameplay. Todo esse aprendizado faz com a Behold Studios consiga apresentar jogos sólidos e que podem despertar, no mínimo, curiosidade do público. sources.title: DMZ — 5 Features to Get Excited for in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4’s New Mode
sources.text: Call of Duty’s upcoming DMZ mode sounds like it’s shaping up to be something special. Set on the new Hajin map and inspired by the events and locations from Modern Warfare 4 ’s Campaign, this open-world combat environment will challenge you to loot, complete objectives, fight both enemies and rival Operators, and extract before everything you’ve earned is lost. Recent intel drops on the official Call of Duty Blog have given us a much clearer picture of what awaits in Hajin when DMZ launches as part of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 . Players who have digitally pre-ordered or pre-purchased Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 can gain Early Access to the game’s Campaign starting Friday, October 16 and all of DMZ starting Tuesday, October 20. The events within DMZ are set after the main MW4 Campaign, leaving a power vacuum in its wake. Now it’s up to you to identify a new, mysterious threat and dismantle its operations across the DMZ through various deployments. From scavenging for crafting materials and experimenting with new technology, to leveling up an Operator, the mode sounds like it offers plenty to look forward to. Here are five features to get excited for when you begin your deployment. The 3D Printer will be available back at the Forward Operating Base (FOB) between deployments and will serve as your primary crafting station to build equipment and upgrades for your loadout before you drop into Hajin. The Call of Duty Blog shares that , as you progress through the DMZ, you’ll unlock new crafting recipes to create more powerful equipment – as well as upgrades to the 3D Printer and even the Forward Operating Base itself. Recipes can also be found on deployments and, presuming you extract in one piece, you can then craft those items for your Operator back at the FOB. When focused on crafting new equipment, the two key things you’ll be looking for when looting on deployments will be Resources and 3D Printer Ingredients – these are the two types of main elements to craft all items. There are four basic Resources to find during a deployment: Synthetics, Electronics, Chemicals, and Metals, automatically broken down from looted items, into your Backpack and Stash. 3D Printer Ingredients are rarer materials found in specific areas of Hajin and are valuable as an ingredient to make a new Item. Examples include Binding Catalyst, Biomaterials, Detonators, and Control Units, to name a few. Once you have enough of these two types of materials, you can select how many copies of an item you want to craft at once, then choose where crafted items go: send completed items directly to your Stash for later or equip them directly to your Operator to quickly prepare for the next deployment. Having this flexibility in how you want to engage the enemy during your deployment can open a variety of experiences in DMZ and can make each deployment feel like it matters, even if you come back to the FOB with zero kills to your name – at least you’ve got handful of electronics or a comms module to make it worth your time. Extraction shooters are always more engaging when every deployment has a clear purpose. That’s not going to be problem with DMZ as it will offer three ways to deploy: Story Missions, Dynamic Operations, and Free Roam. Of those, Story Missions and Dynamic Operations are two that really stand out with their defined objectives and high-tier rewards. According to the Call of Duty Blog , Story Missions will feature narrative-led deployments that you can complete and replay, though some remain locked until prerequisites are met. Each entry provides briefing intel, required objectives, and rewards – usually high-value gear and DMZ Cash – along with options for a random mission and additional milestone rewards. Dynamic Operations, meanwhile, give squads multiple goals to pursue within the DMZ. After deploying, you choose an operation and complete its objectives to earn DMZ XP, Cash, and the ability to call in a Supply Drop filled with unpredictable loot. That extra payoff adds anticipation to every successful Op while making Dynamic Operations a promising source of both Cash and XP. Persistent Operators may be DMZ’s most exciting feature because they allow Hajin to leave a lasting mark on you. You’ll begin with two Operator slots, and unlock a third as you progress through DMZ levels. Each Operator then grows stronger by surviving deployments and earning DMZ XP. Each successful exfil levels up your Operator’s Dog Tags, and this is the key to gaining Trait Points for your Operator. You can invest those points across the Warfighter, Scout, and Survivalist Trait Trees, creating a meaningful choice between specialization and flexibility: with a maximum of 18 points to earn, and a choice of over 60 Trait Points to augment your Operator, you can tailor each Operator to your skills and preferred role. For example, Warfighter Traits include Combat Resistance, Quick Fix, and Viper Sense; Scout Traits include improved Thermal Padding, UAV Upgrade, and Field Crafting; while Survivalist Traits include Faster and Free Revives, increased Consumable Duration, and many more. But here’s where it gets dicey: if an Operator fails to extract and becomes MIA, you must either recover them with DMZ Cash or dismiss them. Because recovery costs rise with Trait investment, bringing back a high-level Operator becomes increasingly expensive. Recovered Operators keep their Traits but lose their gear, putting real weight behind every deployment. The chase for loot is at the heart of every extraction shooter, and DMZ makes each haul matter beyond the current deployment. Returning to base with a pack full of supplies doesn’t just feel rewarding – it improves your chances of success the next time you enter Hajin. Once you drop into a deployment, looting should be a top priority. sources.title: DMZ for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 being released early, but Infinity Ward shoots down PvE hopes
sources.text: In yet another surprising move for Call of Duty, Modern Warfare 4 studio Infinity Ward has announced that the game's extraction shooter mode, DMZ, will be released prior to the game's official launch. DMZ will be available starting 20th October for players who pre-order a copy digitally. Modern Warfare 4 now effectively has three release dates. The campaign unlocks 16th October , DMZ four days later on the 20th, and the full launch - which is when multiplayer will be playable - arrives 23rd October. Though Infinity Ward has offered campaign early access with other Modern Warfare titles in the past, doing the same for DMZ - a multiplayer mode - is certainly new. It's a potentially shrewd move, allowing DMZ to capture streamers and generate excitement about the game ahead of its release over an entire week, with a big blip every few days. It also allows players curious about DMZ to play it without feeling they ought to be making progress in multiplayer instead. Seeing as DMZ has its own separate progression , however, players who jump in early could potentially have an advantage come launch if they manage to accrue many items, not to mention the map knowledge they would get from simply spending more time playing. Separately, Infinity Ward hosted a Reddit Q&A focusing on DMZ , and the question of a PvE-only playlist came up. If you're unfamiliar, a recent first-look gameplay video showed an option for Single Squad Mission in DMZ, which players took to mean a mode free from other players. However, the option disappeared in a follow-up trailer, leading to confusion. So what's going on there? Infinity Ward has an explanation, albeit an unconvincing one. "The playlist you saw is a developer playlist that was never intended to be for public use, it lets our team load into a match alone to work," the developer answered . "In the shipping game, players choose to be solo by turning off squad fill, but it's not guaranteed to be only solos in that lobby." I'm not convinced. Though it's obviously possible for Single Squad to be a dev-only mode, they typically don't require bespoke icons. It's also curious that Infinity Ward didn't blur the image to cover that bit of it, which is commonly done in these sorts of behind-the-scenes videos of gameplay footage, whenever the camera captures something we're not supposed to see. Modern Warfare 4 officially launches 23rd October on PC, PS5, Xbox Series X/S and Switch 2 .

sources.title: Developer Goes Into Debt Spending $1,000 A Day To Keep Steam Demo For AI-Fueled Driving Sim Going
sources.text: Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is an upcoming DMV simulator where players, riding passenger, instruct a chaotic young student to pass their exam. Developers Easy Fox are embracing AI for the project, the titular sister a live chat bot that the player is instructing. Beyond contention for the tech, Easy Fox are finding that the mere demo for the game is proving to be problematic, as accounting for the token usage is forcing them into debt . “Over the past month, the number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold,” reads the Steam pageâs latest update . “Thank you so much for giving our game far more attention than we ever expected. This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably.” As the update explains, the game originally patched players through to a chat bot operating on Googleâs Gemini. With no cost barrier between them and the curious, players of the demo were triggering limit-use errors, Google informing Easy Fox that thereâs no easy way out. Switching to the competing OpenAI model, while hoping to finding a fix with Gemini, is proving to be the least of their problems. Easy Fox says the surge of players has forced them to take out a bank loan to keep the demo operating. Maintaining the demo is apparently costing them more than $1,000 a day, which they admit they will have to factor into pricing the final product. While a number of game developers have flocked to AI to create in-game assets and code on the back-end, Teach My Little Sister is a more unique case. Leveraging an agent for sustained real-time gameplay, the game has found an expensive way to recreate what Lifeline and Hey You, Pikachu! accomplished over 20 years ago. “We want to continue operating the demo and would love for more people to enjoy it,” writes Easy Fox. “However, we are a small team of four, and financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release. We have not made that decision at this time.” The update also addresses complaints that, even in a game based around calamity, the AI fueled sister is not following instructions as desired. While a microcosm of it, the financial strain is an amusing illustration of one of AIâs biggest white elephant. That is, no oneâs sure how to make money off of it. While proliferating in short video content, horrifying fast food posters and visual assets devs “meant to take out,” the firms themselves are running purely on investments, not generating profit. The amount of resources needed to keep these computers burning continually outweighs what the public is otherwise willing to spend to see SpongeBob murder Shrek . Over the last year, AI firms have been forced to adjust, adding new premiums to their service, the so-called “tokenpocalypse.” With the global economy now held hostage by the industry, the burdens of the tech continue to put people on edge. Easy Fox are being taught a swift lesson on something the global population is likely going to learn the hard way. Donât miss the latest reviews, news and tips. Sign up for our free newsletter. sources.title: The developer of an AI-powered driving instruction simulator is spending $1,000 per month just to keep its demo running
sources.text: Teach My Little Sister How to Drive centres around a costly chatbot. One of the many ways AI will (supposedly) revolutionise the games industry is facilitating highly reactive NPCs via LLM-powered chatbots. Yet so far, only a handful of games like Where Winds Meet have attempted to implement the tech, and the results have been less than spectacular. But there might also be another reason why relatively few games feature LLM-powered NPCs, which is that powering such chatbots can be costly, as recently demonstrated by the developers of an upcoming driving instructor simulator As reported by FRVR (via Kotaku ) Teach My Little Sister How To Drive is a comic simulation game in which you coach your virtual sibling on driving technique from the comfort of the passenger seat. The twist is that behind your sister's dinner-plate eyes is an LLM chatbot (currently powered by an OpenAI model, though the developers intend to use Gemini for the final release) In the role of instructor, players can both converse with the chatbot and issue vocal instructions such as "turn left here", to which the bot will respond accordingly. At least, that's the theory. Developer Easy Fox released a demo for Teach My Little Sister How To Drive back in February, but in the past month the game has seen a surge in players, which has had an interesting knock-on effect for the demo. "The number of demo players has grown more than twentyfold," Easy Fox explained in a Steam post , adding. "This growth has also increased our operating costs considerably." Easy Fox goes on to explain that it is "spending over $1,000 per day on AI services for the demo", as players burn through tokens prompting the LLM by proxy. Easy Fox claims that figure "isn't because each player is particularly expensive to support", but rather that "so many people are playing." As a result of this, Easy Fox has "taken out a bank loan to help keep the demo running". Yet even this may not be sufficient to support the demo long term. "Financial pressure may mean we have to close the demo earlier than expected before the full release," Easy Fox says, though the studio stresses it has "not made that decision at this time". According to FRVR, that twentyfold increase in players amounts to 450 concurrent. While the overall player numbers will be higher than that, it isn't an enormous figure, and it makes me wonder how financially viable the game will be when it is released. Easy Fox says it will "account for expected AI usage in the game's price". But it also says that players "will not be charged separately for their individual AI token usage after purchasing the game". That might work in the short term, but surely those token costs are going to pile up over time. It's also worth noting that AI token costs are highly unpredictable , with even large companies like Microsoft and Uber struggling to accurately predict the cost and burn rate of their own internal token use. In its Steam post, Easy Fox says it's looking into options like introducing local AI models for players with "sufficiently capable GPUs". But that's only going to be a fraction of the player-base. Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. All of this is aside from whether an AI-powered driving instruction game is a good idea. Personally, I think the fact that it revolves specifically around chatting with another character makes this a more sensible application than in Where Winds Meet, where the chatbots don't factor into the game design in any meaningful way. It's much more reminiscent of early chatbot-based social sim Façade . But the very fact it reminds me of Façade makes me wonder whether the game needs a premium LLM connected to it to achieve its goal. Easy Fox states that current design problems being addressed include "dialogue that feels too artificial and breaks immersion" and "commands being carried out incorrectly, such as turning right when asked to turn left." All of which seems like it could be solved with a good voice actor and a sufficiently rich dialogue system. Easy Fox plans to release the full game in January next year, so we'll find out exactly how the finances stack up then. 2026 games : All the upcoming games Best PC games : Our all-time favorites Free PC games : Freebie fest Best FPS games : Finest gunplay Best RPGs : Grand adventures Best co-op games : Better together Rick has been fascinated by PC gaming since he was seven years old, when he used to sneak into his dad's home office for covert sessions of Doom. He grew up on a diet of similarly unsuitable games, with favourites including Quake, Thief, Half-Life and Deus Ex. Between 2013 and 2022, Rick was games editor of Custom PC magazine and associated website bit-tech.net . But he's always kept one foot in freelance games journalism, writing for publications like Edge, Eurogamer, the Guardian and, naturally, PC Gamer. stories.title: Entenda os 5 diferentes finais de Silent Hill: Townfall
stories.summary: O final de Townfall é determinado por algumas ações ao longo do jogo

sources.name: Voxel
sources.title: Entenda os 5 diferentes finais de Silent Hill: Townfall
sources.text: Silent Hill: Townfall , o novo spin-off desenvolvido pela Screen Burnem parceria com a Konami, chega para expandir o universo da franquia em um cenário inédito . Desta vez, estamos na isolada ilha escocesa de St. Amelia, em 1996. O protagonista, Simon Ordell, é convocado de volta à cidade para “colocar as coisas em ordem”, mas encontra apenas uma névoa densa cobrindo ruas aparentemente abandonadas. Apesar de não se passar na cidade famosa da franquia, o tipo de contexto é basicamente o mesmo. Seguindo a tradição de jogos da série, Townfall não conta com um final único. Em vez disso, as ações do jogador ao longo da campanha determinam qual desfecho a história vai tomar. Para te ajudar a entender melhor o conceito, listamos os todos os finais de Silent Hill: Townfall e te contamos o que é necessário para conseguir cada um deles. Confira! Como revelado previamente pelos desenvolvedores, o jogo conta com 5 finais diferentes, sendo que 2 são secretos. Assim como em jogos anteriores da série, as decisões tomadas pelo jogador ao longo da aventura é que definem o desfecho, até para que o final pareça coerente com a experiência vivida durante a partida. Não existe uma escolha explícita em algum momento marcante do enredo que define isso, já que o final é determinado por alguns elementos diferentes. O sistema acompanha o comportamento do jogador durante toda a partida, incluindo o quanto ele explora e investiga St. Amelia e o quão agressivo ele é ao ser confrontado por inimigos, em contraste com evitar ou fugir dos combates. Essa abordagem lembra diretamente o clássico Silent Hill 2 , em que o final também refletia padrões de comportamento e não escolhas de diálogo, por exemplo. Dos 5 desfechos possíveis , 3 estão disponíveis já na primeira vez que você zera a campanha , sem necessidade de repetir o jogo. Já os outros 2 finais secretos exigem uma segunda campanha jogada no modo New Game Plus. Esses 3 finais “normais” são chamados de Justice, Forever e Abandoned e são considerados os desfechos principais da trama de Simon. Eles são determinados exclusivamente pela relação entre quantos inimigos o jogador elimina durante a partida e quantas descobertas, como pistas e documentos, ele coleta ao longo do caminho. O tempo de jogo ou uso de itens de cura não influencia nesse resultado. Também é bom mencionar que que esse equilíbrio entre mortes e descobertas afeta apenas a cena final antes dos créditos, sem alterar outras cenas ou a progressão da história ao longo da campanha. Até por isso, você é que tem lembrar de como quer abordar o jogo para conseguir o final desejado. Conforme mencionamos, além dos 3 finais principais, o jogo reserva 2 desfechos extras classificados como secretos , chamados de Dog e Sci-fi. Quem é fã veterano da franquia Silent Hill sabe que esses são finais absolutamente clássicos e colocados no jogo apenas como uma brincadeira extra para o jogador se divertir. Por serem uma piada, é necessário zerar o game uma vez para conseguir um final sério e, então, zerá-lo uma segunda vez no New Game Plus para ter acesso aos desfechos secretos. Como explicado acima, o sistema de finais de Townfall não depende de escolhas de diálogo ou momentos de decisão específicos, mas sim do comportamentos do jogador ao longo de toda a campanha. Para facilitar, nós listamos o que é necessário para cada um. O final Justice é considerado por muitos como o desfecho “bom” da história. Ele é obtido ao final de uma campanha em que o número de descobertas, na forma de pistas e documentos coletados, é significativamente maior do que o número de inimigos eliminados. A boa notícia é que é possível ter dezenas de eliminações e ainda assim alcançar esse final, até porque alguns confrontos ao longo da aventura são praticamente inevitáveis. Por isso, só tente ter certeza de que a quantidade de descobertas seja bem superior. O final Forever é tratado como o desfecho “normal” do jogo. Ele surge quando a quantidade de descobertas é apenas ligeiramente maior do que a quantidade de eliminações ao término da campanha. Diferente do Justice, aqui a margem entre pistas coletadas e inimigos mortos é bem mais estreita, exigindo um equilíbrio mais cuidadoso por parte do jogador ao longo da aventura. Já o Abandoned é considerado o final “ruim” da história. Ele ocorre sempre que o número de inimigos eliminados supera o número de descobertas feitas até o fim do jogo. Para quem opta por um estilo de jogo mais agressivo, ignorando documentos e pistas em favor do combate direto, esse desfecho é praticamente garantido. O final “Dog” é um dos desfechos secretos, exclusivos do New Game Plus. Ele é desbloqueado ao encontrar três moedas especiais espalhadas por diferentes áreas da cidade durante a nova campanha. Com as moedas em mãos, você precisa depositá-las em cofres em formato de cachorro, ligados a uma instituição de cães-guia presente no cenário do jogo. Completar essa sequência de itens substitui o final principal que o jogador obteria normalmente. O Sci-fi é o segundo final secreto, também restrito ao New Game Plus. Para obtê-lo, é necessário interagir com três livros específicos escondidos em diferentes pontos da campanha, resolver um quebra-cabeça de porta usando um código, e por fim utilizar um item especial obtido nesse processo em um painel eletrônico próximo ao fim da aventura. Diferente dos demais finais, o Sci-fi é acionado antes da batalha final, pulando completamente esse confronto e levando direto ao desfecho. Se não quiser spoilers sobre os finais de Silent Hill: Townfall, é melhor pular essa parte do nosso guia! No final “Justice”, Simon consegue encarar os traumas do seu passado de frente, encontrando uma resolução pacífica e libertadora para a sua culpa. No final “Forever”, o protagonista se recusa a aceitar os fatos totalmente e decide permanecer preso na névoa e nas memórias da ilha. No final Abandoned, dominado pela raiva e violência, Simon sucumbe totalmente ao pesadelo e se torna parte do ciclo de sofrimento do loc
